cues: Joule heat is I squared R t: four times a half times three hundred, six hundred joules, about eighty three times bigger, and always given out.
Reversing the current turns the seven point two joules from heating into cooling, but the six hundred joules stay.
That is why real Peltier coolers use semiconductor pellets, with Peltier coefficients hundreds of times bigger.
